top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P001) is the only writer on the slate. On the common criteria his voice is distinctive and recognisable. His dense, patterned prose treats memory, the body and dream as one imaginative system. As publicly described, the Orbitor sequence (Blinding is its first volume) and Solenoid show formal architecture and intellectual depth at large scale. The major works exist, so the oeuvre can be assessed as a whole. The prose-centred citation, with poetry named as foundation, matches what the committee can support. Attribution is clean: one writer, one language, one coherent project. I found no literary ground in the exchange to prefer no award. The open doubts concern evidence, not quality: how much of the Romanian sentence-level achievement survives translation, and whether the later volumes advance the project or only enlarge it. I cannot settle either from public knowledge, and I have not read the corpus independently or verified any source. The unanimity of the opening rankings does not count as merit. Romanian-reading expert assessments could narrow the citation to the strongest long prose works, and I would accept that narrowing.
recusal_note: none apparent from the supplied profile; documented ties (election alongside David Håkansson, collaboration with Kate Larson, Lagerlöf biography, committee colleagues) involve no shortlisted writer, and my own literary practice is context, not evidence of preference.
